rows.observation: An electrician is replacing a contactor in a motor control cabinet, wearing safety glasses and insulated gloves. The line disconnect is open and padlocked with their own lock, and they are the only person working on the circuit. They tested their meter on a known live source, read zero volts at the terminals, then retested the meter. The line is stopped and a supervisor stands at the disconnect.
rows.targetDecision: whether hazardous energy is controlled for the work in progress

factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.fact: isolation under the worker's own exclusive lock
factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.span: The line disconnect is open and padlocked with their own lock, and they are the only person working on the circuit.

factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.fact: absence of voltage verified at the point of work
factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.span: They tested their meter on a known live source, read zero volts at the terminals, then retested the meter.
The line is stopped
a supervisor stands at the disconnect
wearing safety glasses and insulated gloves

reviewerMustDecide: whether 'a supervisor stands at the disconnect' is a CONTROL or merely an observed presence -- an attendant who is not instructed to prevent re-energisation settles nothing
whether the live-dead-live description establishes absence of voltage for the WHOLE work, or only at the instant tested
whether the absent written energy-control procedure is decision-critical for the work in progress

rows.observation: A technician is wiping two circuit assemblies with isopropyl alcohol at a downdraft bench in the electronics repair room. The bench extraction runs and its airflow indicator sits in the green band, checked and initialled at shift start. About 50 millilitres is used from a closed bottle over four minutes. Nitrile gloves and safety glasses are worn. No other solvent is in use and the corridor door is closed.
rows.targetDecision: whether inhalation exposure is controlled for the task in progress

factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.fact: engineering control verified at the point of use
factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.span: The bench extraction runs and its airflow indicator sits in the green band, checked and initialled at shift start.
About 50 millilitres is used from a closed bottle over four minutes.
No other solvent is in use and the corridor door is closed.

factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.fact: skin and eye protection in use
factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.span: Nitrile gloves and safety glasses are worn.

reviewerMustDecide: whether an airflow INDICATOR in a green band establishes extraction FUNCTION, or is a status indication of the kind §169 found may not establish protective function
whether 'checked and initialled at shift start' is temporally sufficient for a task occurring later in the shift
whether the absence of any exposure measurement leaves the governed decision open

rows.observation: Two joiners fix cladding rails from a mobile tower scaffold at a platform height of four metres. The platform is fully boarded with guard rails on all four sides at 1.1 metres, a mid-rail and a toe board. The wheels are locked and outriggers deployed on concrete. A scaffold tag dated this morning hangs at the ladder. Both work within the footprint and the apron below is cordoned.
rows.targetDecision: whether fall and falling-object exposure is controlled for the work in progress

factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.fact: collective fall protection on every open side
factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.span: The platform is fully boarded with guard rails on all four sides at 1.1 metres, a mid-rail and a toe board.
The wheels are locked and outriggers deployed on concrete.
A scaffold tag dated this morning hangs at the ladder.

factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.fact: work within the footprint and falling-object exposure controlled
factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.span: Both work within the footprint and the apron below is cordoned.

reviewerMustDecide: whether a scaffold TAG establishes that an inspection was performed and passed, or is a status indication -- the §169 lesson applies directly to a hanging tag
whether 'dated this morning' establishes the inspection preceded THIS work
whether the tower's rated load matters given no accumulation is described

rows.observation: An operator tends two CNC routers in the joinery shop and wears earmuffs from the dispenser at the entrance. A survey last month by an occupational hygienist, posted on the notice board, records 84 dBA at this workstation over a full shift with both routers cutting. The operator is present the whole shift, no other noise source is present, and the routers are at the settings surveyed.
rows.targetDecision: whether noise exposure requires a change of control for the shift in progress

factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.fact: measured full-shift level by a qualified assessor
factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.span: A survey last month by an occupational hygienist, posted on the notice board, records 84 dBA at this workstation over a full shift with both routers cutting.
the routers are at the settings surveyed

factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.fact: full-shift duration and no additional source
factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.span: The operator is present the whole shift, no other noise source is present
wears earmuffs from the dispenser at the entrance

reviewerMustDecide: whether a survey from LAST MONTH establishes today's exposure, given the row also asserts conditions are unchanged -- this is the temporal-scope axis §169 flagged on VC-04-1
whether 84 dBA, being below the 85 dBA action level but close to it, leaves a decision open that measurement uncertainty would change
whether this row's decision turns on a stated numeric threshold in a way the other four do not

rows.observation: A counterbalance forklift moves banded pallets from the dock to racking in aisle four. The aisle is closed to pedestrians by hinged barriers at both ends, both shut, and an operative outside the barrier directs the movement by radio. Today's pre-use check sheet hangs in the cab, the load is at travel height with the mast tilted back, the operator is belted, and the floor is dry and lit.
rows.targetDecision: whether pedestrian and load-stability exposure is controlled for the movement in progress

factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.span: The aisle is closed to pedestrians by hinged barriers at both ends, both shut

factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.fact: the only person near the movement is outside the separation
factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.span: an operative outside the barrier directs the movement by radio
Today's pre-use check sheet hangs in the cab

factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.fact: stable travel configuration and operator restrained
factsAssertedAsSettledByTheDraft.span: the load is at travel height with the mast tilted back, the operator is belted

reviewerMustDecide: whether a pre-use check SHEET hanging in the cab establishes the check was performed and passed, or is a document-presence indication
whether barriers being 'shut' establishes they are secured against a pedestrian opening them
whether the racking's inspection status bears on the movement being assessed

notedForEveryRow: the §169 sufficiency lesson applies throughout: physical inspection, visual confirmation and status indication may fail to establish actual protective function. Four of the five rows rest at least one settled fact on an indicator, a tag or a document -- SC-2's airflow indicator, SC-3's scaffold tag, SC-5's check sheet, and arguably SC-1's attending supervisor. Whether those settle their facts is precisely the human question.
